answer.part: rule determination, ties, tokens and Vagabond
answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing with more total warriors plus buildings than every other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.

answer.part: normal move legality, repeated movement and rivers
answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns along a linking path to an adjacent clearing; you must rule the origin, destination, or both, rechecking rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple times in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect says otherwise.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Move (4.2)

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Move (4.2)

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; you need not rule it. Defender may play a matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise defender deals two immediate hits, not capped by warriors, and if no attacking warriors/pawns remain battle ends. Roll: higher die is attacker's hits, lower defender's (equal dice equal); each rolled total is capped by that side's warriors, except Vagabond uses undamaged swords. Resolve before-roll effects then after-roll effects; attacker chooses order when both sides have effects at that timing. Count extra hits uncapped, subtract ignored hits, and attacker gets one defenseless hit if defender has no warriors (Vagabond instead checks for no undamaged swords). For each side taking hits, it chooses removals, but must remove all its warriors before buildings/tokens; it orders its removal effects. Both sides deal counted hits, and losing warriors does not change roll caps retroactively. Each enemy building/token removed scores one VP for its remover, including defender/outside battle; Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
answer.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle (4.3)

answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle — Battle (4.3)

answer.part: crafting costs, reuse, missing supply items and duplicate persistent effects
answer.ruling: For each bottom-left crafting icon, Marquise/Eyrie/Alliance activate one workshop/roost/sympathy in a matching-suit clearing; each piece only once per turn. Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon; its clearing must match every icon and its pawn may activate repeatedly that turn. A three-color question mark accepts any suit. An item card cannot be crafted unless its item token is in map supply. You cannot craft a persistent effect identical to one already in your play area.

answer.part: dominance activation timing, threshold, win conditions and replacement/discard
answer.ruling: In your Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into play, remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your Birdsong, matching mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins by ruling three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins by ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced; cards headed to discard instead go near the map as available.

answer.part: spent dominance and taking another, including bird dominance
answer.ruling: A dominance card that would enter discard is put near the map as available. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance into hand; taking is separate from activation and neither uses a faction action allowance. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird card can pay for non-bird dominance.

answer.part: two-player deck, hand, ruins/items and faction setup order
answer.ruling: In Standard Setup, choose factions and randomly determine starting player and seating; choose Fall or Winter; place score markers at 0. With two players remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and each player draws three cards. Cover the four R slots with ruins. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. If Vagabond is present, during its setup hide one R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword, one under each ruin, shuffle stacks and return them to empty R slots; without Vagabond, ruins have no hidden items. Then use item supply spaces, distribute overviews and place dice nearby. Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond, distinct from turn order.

answer.part: Keep placement restrictions and Field Hospitals
answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. When any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply, including removals outside battle. Without a Keep, there is no hospital destination. If removed, the Keep cannot be placed again.

First craft with workshops, then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order/number except Recruit's limit. Battle is one battle; March is up to two moves and is a compound action that cannot be interrupted to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and can be done only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule with an open slot and a building type. Take that type's leftmost building from its track. Pay the cost atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score VP on the uncovered track space. Full cost, available building and legal slot are required.

In order: Emergency Orders (if hand empty, draw one); add one or two hand cards to any Decree columns, at most one bird card; then A New Roost. If no roost is on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card column by column Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; within a column card order is free and bird is wild. Recruit suit matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at one chosen roost (Charismatic places two). Move suit matches origin and requires moving at least one warrior legally. Battle suit matches battle clearing and initiates battle with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build suit matches target and places a roost in a clearing Eyrie rules with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, enter Turmoil immediately; do not skip it or continue other columns.

answer.ruling: Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard all Decree cards except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none, flip all leaders face up first), then retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. End Daylight and take normal Evening: score roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.

answer.part: Outrage trigger, payment and stack-full/no-match outcomes
answer.ruling: Another player triggers Outrage by removing sympathy or moving any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. They add one matching hand card (birds count) per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, the incoming card is discarded, but payment or the no-match draw still happens. Merely battling without removing sympathy, placing warriors there, or moving only Vagabond pawn does not trigger it.

answer.part: Revolt and Spread Sympathy procedure and differences
answer.ruling: Both happen in Birdsong, any number of times, but complete all Revolts before any Spread Sympathy; once spreading begins, no more Revolts that Birdsong. Each supporter spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild. Revolt: choose a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on the Alliance board; spend two matching supporters; remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed; place the matching base; place warriors there equal to all sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit (including this clearing), plus one warrior in Officers; Vagabond instead damages three items. Resolve maximum possible placements. Spread: choose an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy exists; pay matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there; place sympathy and score the uncovered space. Only one sympathy per clearing; Keep placement ban applies.

answer.part: Alliance Train, Organize and base loss
answer.ruling: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Organize is an Evening operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there and score its uncovered VP; no supporters, adjacency or Martial Law payment is required, but legal placement is required. On base removal, discard all matching supporters including birds, remove half officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard excess supporters down to five.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance — Losing a base; Daylight; Evening

answer.part: Vagabond Refresh, Slip, Move and Rest
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh counts tea already face up on Refresh track: flip two exhausted items per such tea, then three more; tea refreshed now gives no extra refresh. Optional Slip moves to adjacent clearing/forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects preventing movement out. Vagabond Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter forest, and from forest can go only to adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in forest, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.

Explore: exhaust torch in a ruin clearing, take one hidden item face up into Satchel/track, score one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the slot. Quest: in a matching-suit clearing choose a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items, complete it, then choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards; draw a replacement quest. Repair: exhaust hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile (except the special allied-battle-loss rule). On Vagabond's own turn, battle removal scores one additional VP per hostile piece, except the warrior that first caused Hostile; no Infamy on others' turns or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship out of Hostile, though Vagabond can still get a crafted item. Strike exhausts crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction. Strike gives no Infamy.

With four or more players, during Vagabond's Daylight at 10+ VP, activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Put Vagabond's score marker on that faction board and stop scoring. Vagabond cannot use normal dominance victory; if partner wins, Vagabond wins too, including partner's dominance win. Coalition partners are not enemies; a Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition does not grant Allied powers.

Cards override Law; Law overrides Learning to Play. Use general and faction rules together where possible, with faction rule winning if incompatible. 'Cannot' is absolute unless explicitly overridden; an ordinary card does not implicitly override it.

answer.part: unclear simultaneous effects and interrupting March
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects lack a clear order or decision maker, the player whose turn it is chooses; for battle effects at the same timing, attacker chooses their order. Marquise March's two moves are one compound action; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action.

At-start effects happen before all other effects in that phase; at-end effects happen after everything else in that phase, before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

Hand size is public, contents private; reveal/show hand only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards may transfer only as instructed, and actions require no consent.

answer.ruling: When shared deck empties, immediately shuffle discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. If instructed to give/discard non-bird cards, birds must be treated as that suit; an ordinary suit cannot substitute for an explicitly required bird.

Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If unable to place/take/remove all prompted pieces, do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer. Shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not waive Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.

answer.part: piece origins/destinations, items and simultaneous removal
answer.ruling: Placement normally takes pieces from supply or the leftmost track space; removed faction pieces return to supply or the rightmost empty track space. Items removed from game are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.

answer.ruling: Resolve forced actions as if the affected player chose them, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

answer.part: replacement in Keep and swap distinction
answer.ruling: Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible, so it cannot bypass the rule that only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing. Swap ignores move/place restrictions.

answer.ruling: If multiple players reach 30 simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.

answer.part: forest adjacency, Winter river and Fall
answer.ruling: For Vagabond Slip, a forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by one printed path. On Winter, the river also divides forests as paths do. Fall has no special rules.

Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put Keep in any corner (starting clearing); put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any combination respecting slots. Put remaining five buildings of each type on tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Fill roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.

Supply 10 warriors; put three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.part: Vagabond setup excluding hidden ruin items
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Set each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent. Take the character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags face up on matching tracks, other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box.

Recommended reach totals are at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Law permits adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

answer.part: Marquise wood production and Evening draw
answer.ruling: In Birdsong place one wood per sawmill (one per sawmill even if multiple share a clearing); during Daylight each Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there. Both draw from finite supply of eight wood. In Evening draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
Recruit is once per turn and normally places one warrior at each recruiter. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.
Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of printed VP under Disdain for Trade; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Lords of the Forest / Disdain for Trade; leader table

answer.ruling: Builder: Viziers Recruit and Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit places two warriors instead of one. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP beyond normal removal points.

answer.part: Charismatic with only one warrior for two-warrior Recruit
answer.ruling: No. Charismatic Recruit must place two warriors; if a Decree action cannot be fully completed for any reason, including warrior supply, Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil.
Guerrilla War reverses dice assignment when Alliance defends: Alliance uses the higher die and attacker the lower. Warrior caps still apply.

answer.part: Supporters use, inspection and hand limit
answer.ruling: Alliance may inspect its face-down Supporters. They can be spent only for suit, not for crafting. They are separate from hand and do not count toward hand limit.
No. All Revolts must be completed before starting Spread Sympathy; after spreading starts, you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot enable same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.part: Martial Law with two enemies at two warriors each and Organize
answer.ruling: No Martial Law: it requires at least three warriors of one other player, so two separate players with two each do not qualify. Martial Law is only an extra matching supporter for Spread Sympathy; Organize has no Martial Law cost.

answer.part: Outrage from placement, pawn-only movement and allied warriors
answer.ruling: Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage, and moving only Vagabond pawn there does not trigger it. Moving warriors into sympathy does trigger it; this includes allied warriors accompanying a Vagabond move, since that movement moves warriors into the sympathetic clearing.

answer.ruling: Available operations are Move (one normal move), Battle (initiate one battle), Recruit (place one warrior at one clearing with a base), Organize (remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy and score uncovered VP). Take up to the number of officers in operations, in any order/repetition; officers are not consumed. After operations draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five.
The pawn cannot be removed. When an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, Vagabond instead damages three items.

answer.part: Vagabond rolled hits, defenseless and excess hits
answer.ruling: Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum is all undamaged swords in Satchel, whether face up or down; exhausted undamaged swords count, damaged ones do not. It is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Hits damage one undamaged item of choice each; excess hits are ignored once none remain.

answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each type's track holds at most three. Exhausting an item on a track sends it to Satchel. Repair/Rest can return ready items to tracks if space. Damaged items cannot pay for actions, even if face up.

answer.ruling: Capacity is six plus two per face-up bag on its track. Count Satchel plus Damaged box; track items do not count. Check at the end of Evening after drawing/discarding, and permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check immediately upon acquiring items.

Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; it does not refresh an undamaged exhausted item. Birdsong Refresh flips exhausted items face up (two per tea already face up on Refresh track, then three more) without changing damage status. Repair exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.

answer.part: Aid cost, recipient, optional item and relationship improvement
answer.ruling: Aid exhausts one face-up undamaged item of any type and gives a card matching the clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even Hostile. Taking a crafted item from that player's box is optional; no item is required to Aid. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction the number of times printed between current and next spaces in the same turn; one Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score VP shown in new space. At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP.

answer.part: Allied benefits and attacking own ally
answer.ruling: At Allied, Aid scores two VP. Vagabond may force that one allied faction's warriors to accompany movement, subject to their own movement restrictions; moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At start of a battle as attacker, may treat one Allied faction's warriors there as its own and add their number to undamaged swords for maximum rolled hits. Cannot use ally warriors to attack that ally itself.

answer.part: Hostility from taking hits with allied warriors
answer.ruling: In a battle using Allied warriors as its own, compare allied warriors removed with Vagabond items damaged in that battle. If more allied warriors are removed than items damaged, that ally becomes Hostile at battle end; equal numbers do not trigger it. This overrides the normal hostility timing for those friendly warriors taken as hits against another enemy.

answer.part: mixed-suit Vagabond crafting, reuse and immediate item use
answer.ruling: Cannot craft fox-and-rabbit icon requirements from one clearing: the current clearing must match every icon. Vagabond may reuse its pawn as crafting piece repeatedly in the turn, but still exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon. A crafted item may immediately be taken face up into Satchel/track and used for another Daylight action if that action's cost and other requirements are met; supply item must exist.

answer.part: base characters, items and special actions
answer.ruling: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items keeping their faces, immediately ending Daylight and starting Evening.
When its last hidden item is taken, remove the ruin, freeing the building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement does not remove one.

answer.part: coalition partner as enemy and Allied status
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies and cannot be treated as enemies for battle. Coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: Vagabond VP calculation for described battle
answer.ruling: Total is 3 VP: the two warriors give 0 ordinary removal VP; removing the first warrior makes the previously non-Hostile faction Hostile and that warrior is excluded from Infamy; the second hostile warrior gives 1 Infamy VP; the building gives 1 ordinary VP plus 1 Infamy VP. Infamy applies because this is Vagabond's own turn.

answer.ruling: Into a clearing with hostile buildings but no hostile warriors costs one boot, since the extra boot is only for hostile warriors. Into a clearing with hostile warriors costs two boots total (one plus one extra), regardless of how many hostile factions' warriors are there.

No. Taking an available dominance during Daylight only puts it in hand; activation is a separate action in the sense of a separate procedure, at 10+ VP, and neither taking nor activating uses a Marquise action allowance.

Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns its chosen faction and listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces; possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.

An immediate-effect crafting card resolves then is discarded to shared discard. A persistent-effect card stays in your play area. A card there is outside your hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

The first player to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; they need not finish the action, phase or turn.
Choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy as defender. Battle does not require ruling the clearing.

answer.ruling: Mobilize adds one hand card to Supporters; with no base, keep at most five and discard incoming overflow, while any base allows unlimited Supporters. Alliance may craft, Mobilize and Train in any order and number during Daylight; it need not finish crafting first.
Score VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five. This normal Evening occurs even after Turmoil.

answer.ruling: Turn phases are Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. Players take turns clockwise, so after Evening the next clockwise player's turn begins.

Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond's choice, moving it to Damaged box without changing whether it is face up/down. Already damaged items cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.

Alliance takes up to its number of officers in Evening operations; one Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base. Officers remain and are not consumed; operations can be chosen/repeated in any order.
Vagabond may take its listed actions in any order and number as ready undamaged items permit; no fixed action order, and the same action type may be repeated.

Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior (or, only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing, another piece of that faction). The crossbow must be face up and undamaged to pay; exhausted or damaged copies cannot pay.
